entry.subject: Axle as generator / transformer analogy and battery regeneration path
entry.trigger: Question whether the rotating magnetized Axle creates transformer-like induction and whether resulting electrical energy can be collected into the battery.
result: The underlying physics is Faraday induction. A transformer changes flux electrically; JANUS changes flux at stationary coils mechanically by rotating the magnetic Axle.
With permanent magnets on the Axle and stationary AFPM windings, the system is already a permanent-magnet generator whenever external mechanical torque drives the rotor.
The same coreless AFPM unit can therefore operate as starter motor, RPM controller, regenerative brake and generator through a bidirectional inverter/DC bus.
Bulk eddy currents induced in a copper/brass Axle are not preferred as a collection mechanism; they behave more like an unintended shorted transformer secondary and mainly produce heat and Lenz drag.

If the battery is the only source spinning the Axle, harvesting from the same rotation cannot produce a net gain; electrical loading increases opposing torque and returns less energy than was supplied.
True regenerative battery charge is valid when independently measured hydraulic/external shaft work drives the Axle or when finite rotor kinetic energy is recovered during deceleration.
entry.new_architecture: AUTO_MOTOR_TO_REGEN_CROSSOVER: battery starts Axle -> hydraulic/process assistance reduces motor current -> zero-current crossover -> if external torque exceeds losses, AFPM automatically reverses DC power flow and charges battery.
entry.next_measurement: Measure open-circuit back EMF, torque, DC-bus power, battery Wh, water hydraulic power and B-field together across 60/120/300/600 RPM to locate the real motor-to-zero-to-regeneration crossover.
